item.title: Spectral properties of the magnetic Robin Laplacian on curvilinear half-plane
item.description: arXiv:2609.03783v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We analyse magnetic Robin Laplacian in curvilinear half-plane with a smooth boundary. It is well known that the spectrum of the Robin Laplacian is unstable with respect to boundary deformations. This means that if the boundary is a straight line then the spectrum of the Robin Laplacian is purely essential. From the other hand, the perturbation of the boundary produces eigenvalues below the essential spectrum. In this paper, the Robin-Laplace operator with a compactly supported magnetic field is considered. We prove that the spectrum of the magnetic Robin Laplacian is stable under small and local deformations of the boundary.
item.dc:creator: Diana Barseghyan, Baruch Schneider, Yifan Zhang

item.title: Decay Rates and Domain Dependence of a Coupled Wave-Heat System with Spatially Dependant Heat Coefficients
item.description: arXiv:2609.03980v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study of the long-term behavior of a coupled wave-heat system. The system consists of a wave equation and a heat equation on two adjacent Lipschitz domains coupled by a common interface, with the heat equation being allowed to incorporate spatially dependant coefficients. We first establish strong asymptotic stability independent of the domains and coefficients. To this end, we employ the framework of closure relations, which reduces the spectral analysis of the coupled system to that of a wave equation. Secondly, we analyze non-uniform decay rates for classical solutions to the coupled system. Using methods from the theory of $C_0$-semigroups and a non-orthogonal decomposition of the state space, we reduce the problem to a residual estimate which is independent of the heat domain and heat coefficients, instead depending monotonically on the wave domain and the interface. With this, we are able to extend the known non-uniform decay rates to spatially dependent heat coefficients, yielding logarithmic decay under no assumptions, as well as polynomial decay in one dimensions or under the Geometric Control Condition.
item.dc:creator: Pascal Heymo{\ss}

item.title: A new proof of the Lemmens-Seidel conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2511.03396v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we give a new proof of the Lemmens-Seidel conjecture on the maximum number of equiangular lines with a common angle $\arccos(1/5)$. This conjecture was previously resolved by Cao, Koolen, Lin, and Yu in 2022 through an analysis involving forbidden subgraphs for the smallest Seidel eigenvalue $-5$. Our new proof is based on bounds on eigenvalue multiplicities of graphs with degree no larger than $14$. To control the maximum degree of the graph associated with equiangular lines, we employ a recent inequality of Balla derived by matrix projection techniques. Our strategy also leads to a new proof for the classical result obtained by Lemmens and Seidel in 1973 for the case where the common angle is $\arccos(1/3)$.
item.dc:creator: Chuanyuan Ge, Shiping Liu
